title: Untrimmed output reference and box-method temperature coefficient over -40..125 degC
claim: README.md 'Target specification (DRAFT)' rows 'Output reference' (1.20 V +/-1% untrimmed) and 'Temp coefficient (-40...125 degC)' (< 50 ppm/degC), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Records are PROVISIONAL against the draft spec until issue #1 ratifies it. Measures design/bandgap_core.sch open-circuit, untrimmed (no trim network -- that is issue #13), across process and supply corners with temperature swept continuously inside the deck.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim -- untrimmed spread from local mismatch is issue #12's Monte Carlo)

analyses: meas dc vref27 FIND v(vref) AT=27

measurements.name: vref_27
measurements.note: Untrimmed open-circuit reference at 27 degC, read off the in-deck temperature sweep. Window is the draft spec's 1.20 V +/-1%. 27 degC is not on the 5 degC sweep grid (-40, -35, ... 120, 125), so this is ngspice's linear interpolation between the 25 degC and 30 degC points; on a curve whose total excursion is tens of mV over 165 degC the interpolation error is ~10 uV (< 0.001% of 1.2 V), four orders of magnitude inside the +/-1% window.

measurements.name: vref_min
measurements.note: Minimum of VREF over the -40..125 degC sweep. Bounds are a loose +/-5% sanity band, not the spec window: the spec line is on the 27 degC value and on the TC derived from this excursion. A value outside +/-5% means the curve left the bandgap regime somewhere in the range and the TC number below would be meaningless.

measurements.name: vref_max
measurements.note: Maximum of VREF over the -40..125 degC sweep; same loose sanity band as vref_min.

measurements.name: tc_ppm
measurements.note: Box-method TC: peak-to-peak VREF excursion over -40..125 degC, normalized to VREF(27 degC) and to the 165 degC span. Limit is the draft spec's < 50 ppm/degC target column; the < 20 ppm/degC stretch column is out of scope for wave 1 per DR-001's scope note.

measurements.name: n_temp_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck temperature sweep really produced 34 points (-40..125 degC at 5 degC). If the sweep silently collapsed to a single operating point, the box TC above would read 0 ppm/degC and look like a spectacular pass. This check makes that failure loud.

spread_checks.note: VREF(27 degC) must move by at least 0.1 mV across the process/supply matrix. A dead-flat result across 15 corner points means the corner include or the supply param is not reaching the simulator.

notes: Temperature is swept INSIDE the deck (dc temp -40 125 5) because the box method needs the peak-to-peak excursion of a continuous curve; a three-point outer axis would miss the curvature extremum, which for a bandgap generally sits between the endpoints. The runner is therefore invoked with --temp 27 --subset-reason; process and supply run in full (5 x 3 = 15 points).

Grid resolution is 5 degC (34 points), not 1 degC. Rationale: the VREF(T) characteristic is smooth and near-quadratic, so a 5 degC grid can miss the true extremum by at most 2.5 degC. With this core's measured curvature (~30 mV of excursion over 165 degC, i.e. a quadratic coefficient of order 4e-6 V/degC^2) that costs at most ~30 uV of peak-to-peak, under 0.1% of the reported TC. Each temperature step forces ngspice to re-evaluate the whole PDK model set's temperature-dependent parameters, which is what makes the sweep expensive; 1 degC resolution buys nothing measurable for ~5x the runtime.
The corner axes above declare the full PVT matrix so the manifest stays the canonical statement of what the claim requires and the subset is visible as a subset in the record.
